title: A day of renunciation
hook: plain food, nothing to watch, and an old phrase for living lightly.
tomorrow: you've given, kept and let go. what's left to see clearly?

segments.voice: Six lines from the week. A day of giving starts with noticing. Good conduct, a gift to strangers. Kept under pressure. A clean day. Let it go. And yesterday, Temiya: he renounced the throne, and chose his moment to speak.
screen: `A DAY OF GIVING.` → `GOOD CONDUCT.` → `KEPT UNDER PRESSURE.` → `A CLEAN DAY.` → `LET IT GO.` → `HE RENOUNCED THE THRONE.`

segments.voice: Some people try a no-spend weekend, or a day without screens. So what is a whole day like with plain food and no entertainment? The Buddha's teaching on kindness has an old phrase for the kind of person who could manage it, and it's not grim at all. In Pali: santussako ca subharo ca. Content, and easy to support.
screen: `A NO-SPEND WEEKEND.` → `PLAIN FOOD, NOTHING TO WATCH.` → `CONTENT, AND EASY TO SUPPORT.`

segments.voice: The line comes from the Metta Sutta, the discourse on loving-kindness. Before it gets to wishing all beings well, it describes the person who does the wishing: able, upright, gentle, content and easy to support, with few duties, living lightly. Contentment is listed right beside kindness, as if a person who needs less has more room for others. The Dhammapada says it outright: contentment is the greatest wealth. That's what a day of renunciation tests. Plain food, so taste isn't running the day. No entertainment, so attention comes home. The first hours can feel long. That's not failure; it's the extra noise draining out. This week's whole block sits inside it. You notice what others need, because you're not busy feeding yourself. You keep the precepts more easily, because there's less to grab for. You let go, a little, and find out what it trades for. A simple day isn't a lesser day. It's the same day with the clutter out of it.
screen: `CONTENT, AND EASY TO SUPPORT.` · `CONTENTMENT, THE GREATEST WEALTH.` · `THE NOISE DRAINS OUT.` · `THE WHOLE WEEK, IN ONE DAY.` · then, large: `SIMPLE DAY.`

segments.voice: Look at what's around you right now and count three things that are already enough: the seat holding you, the water within reach, the light in the room. Name each one quietly. Then sit with the word enough for the rest of the bell.
A day of renunciation: plain food, no entertainment, and a mind content with little. Living lightly, for one day.
The line for today: simple day, the same day with the clutter out. Two weeks done; see you on the next page.

screen: `DAY 1554 COUNTS.` → `THE TEN PERFECTIONS · DAY 9 OF 30.` → `TOMORROW: YOU'VE GIVEN, KEPT AND LET GO. WHAT'S LEFT TO SEE?`

howItsDone: Some lay Buddhists keep days of simplicity, sometimes on observance days, eating plainly and setting aside entertainment; the Metta Sutta, chanted in Theravada lands, names contentment among the qualities of a kind person.

fork.setup: your cousin is doing a "simple day" and posts every plain meal online for likes. going by today's lesson, what's off?
options: nothing: plain food is plain food, posted or not.
the plainness has become a show; living lightly doesn't need an audience.

original.note: Pali: contentment, being satisfied with little.

trapdoor: what you thought: a day of going without, just to prove you can.
what it means: plain food, no entertainment and a mind content with little, so the day has room in it.
what a scholar hears: Sutta Nipata 1.8 (Karaniya Metta Sutta): santussako ca subharo ca, appakicco ca sallahukavutti; Dhammapada 204 on contentment as wealth.

chat.says: trying ông's "simple day": plain rice, no shows, no playlist. it's 2pm and i'm SO bored. doing it wrong?
options: Not wrong. That's the extra noise draining out. Content with little is the point.
Yes. If it isn't peaceful right away, the simple day hasn't worked at all.
Add one show to break it up. Simple just means less of everything, not none.
chat.meaning: The Metta Sutta's kind person is content and easy to support. A simple day lets the clutter drain out, even if it feels long.
